messages:
Alex K: quick hit from yesterday's smoke — seeing OOMs on medium-concurrency runs when kernel-selector picks the "fast-attn" kernel. Profiling shows large workspace spikes that collide with logits slab during KV-heavy chat workloads.
Priya S: ugh. do you have the flamegraph? can you paste the peak alloc trace?
Alex K: pasted below (trimmed):
```
# peak GPU alloc timeline
196MB activation_pool
512MB fast-attn.workspace
256MB logits_slab
KV cache ~300MB
-> total exceeded by ~200MB at step t+42
```
Alex K: note that this only happens when batch size is 8-12 and KV hits are > 250MB. small batches ok, big batches auto-switch to compact kernel.
Jorge M: sounds like eviction thrash between logits_slab and activation buffers. hybrid eviction currently prefers freeing logits first, but fast-attn kernel wants contiguous workspace so it pins a large chunk. when eviction fails we late-free activations which blocks kernels -> OOM.
Emily R: can we make kernel-selector aware of current free workspace instead of just sequence length profile? i.e. prefer kernels with smaller peak if free < X.
Ryan L: +1. we already have a heuristics table but you can push a quick guard: if free_gpu_mem < 600MB && kv_usage > 200MB => prefer compact kernel. patch is tiny.
Priya S: also think we should change slab eviction order to account for reuse score. logits slabs with recent hits should be scored higher and evicted last. currently eviction is FIFO-ish.
Jorge M: agreed. propose two changes for canary: 1) kernel-selector guard (Ryan's) 2) adjust logits slab score to include recency+prefetch_hint. third smaller change: avoid eager-zeroing of newly allocated workspace for fast-attn when !needs_zero -> saves ~50-60MB transient.
Alex K: canary sounds good. let's avoid big allocator rewrites in canary. we want minimal surface to toggle.
Emily R: I'll run canary on r2-small pool. can we add a test that reproduces KV-heavy trace? I have a script that hits KV with many short prompts.
Priya S: @Emily R paste the script in #eng-runtime-tests? also add env var to enable slab scoring: `RD_POOL_SLAB_SCORING=v2`.
Emily R: will do. launching canary now with flags: `RD_KERNEL_GUARD=1 RD_POOL_MODE=hybrid RD_POOL_SLAB_SCORING=v2 RD_EAGER_ZERO=0`
infra-bot: deploy queued: canary r2-small -> 5 hosts. triggered by Emily R. (deploy id: d-2026-03-18-42)
Emily R: canary is live. perf endpoint: https://perf.redwood.internal/canaries/d-2026-03-18-42/trace
Ryan L: if the canary passes, let's keep kernel-guard for 2 weeks then roll to larger pools. also consider exposing thresholds as dynamic metrics in console.
Jorge M: one more note: KV cache eviction currently steals from slab with a blunt scalar. we should prefer reclamation of staging scratchpad pages first (they're less likely to be reused across timesteps). small change but helps.
Alex K: good point. add that to the followup ticket.
Priya S: recorded issue -> #ENGRT-1534 (buffer-reclaim-priority). assigning to Jorge.
Jorge M: ack. i'll instrument more traces: add `allocator.debug=1` to canary and pull max-res trace after 6h.
Emily R: early signal: canary reduced OOMs to 0 in first 200 runs. latency 95p slightly up (~25ms) for some prompts but overall throughput stable.
Alex K: nice. keep monitoring for 24h. if stable we merge kernel-guard and slab-scoring to canary fast-path.
Ryan L: also add a rollback plan: pin kernel-selector to "compact-workspace" for r2-large if needed.
Emily R: noted. I'll post summary in #eng-runtime after 24h and tag infra for rollout plan. :thumbsup:
Alex K: thanks team. small wins but avoids touching allocator internals for now.
infra-bot: canary finished: 5 hosts, 24h completed, no OOMs reported. logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/d-2026-03-18-42
Emily R: merging kernel-guard to staging branch now. will schedule broader canary next week.
Priya S: followups: add a perf metric for "workspace headroom" and a lint in kernel-selector tests to simulate low-headroom.
Jorge M: creating perf PR with traces + new slab scoring algorithm.
Alex K: wrap up: short-term fix = kernel selector guard + slab scoring v2 + avoid eager-zero; medium-term = allocator worklet reclamation + prioritized scratchpad eviction.
Ryan L: love it.
Alex K: closing thread. thanks all.
